32661-rembrandt-van-rijn:
Malcolm Bell surveys Rembrandt van Rijn in three parts: the man, the painter, and the etcher. Nine chapters trace his birth and training, his years of wealth, and his later decline. A catalogue of works and a list of plates round out the volume.

Bell weighs the portraits, the biblical scenes, and the etchings, noting both Rembrandt's bold handling and his faults. The book gives a compact life and a guide to the art, from early portraits of his parents to the late work made in harder times. Bell also prints a chronological table, so readers can place each work in the painter's life.
britannica-1911-huygens-sir-constantijn:
Sir Constantijn Huygens (1596-1687), a Dutch poet and diplomat, is the subject of an article in the 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica. He was born at the Hague in September 1596. His father was secretary to the state council and a man of weight in public life. The child was trained in every polite skill of the age.

The article marvels at the breadth of his gifts. Before he was seven he could speak French with ease. A tutor taught him Latin, and he soon mastered verse in the classic forms. He had good looks, great strength, and skill at the lute, at painting, and at engraving. In 1616 he went with his elder brother to the university at Leiden. Two years later he travelled to London with an English ambassador, then studied at Oxford in the great library there.
